# Senlay - full LLM and agent context

Senlay is a physical-world intelligence infrastructure beta for autonomous systems, robotics and AI applications. It returns available environmental observations and model context for a coordinate with source, time, distance, disagreements and unknowns where available.

Contributor pilots test whether signed station observations can improve local coverage. Access is manually agreed and limited; registering a station does not grant unlimited API access. Source rights, quotas and scope must be confirmed. See https://senlay.cloud/network.html and https://senlay.cloud/robotics/. No paying customers or provider partnerships are claimed.

SmartSurf (https://smartsurf.cloud/) is the product origin and a reference experience. It is not proof of robotics demand, paid Senlay traction or completed field validation.

Senlay uses environmental providers and station networks as optional data inputs where access and rights permit. Its intended output combines available source provenance, type, distance, timestamp, observation age, model disagreement, optional `risk_event` records, and an agent-ready `context_string`. Differences from other providers require a dated, reproducible comparison; no blanket claim is made that weather APIs omit provenance or conceal model origin.


## Current availability and scope

Senlay is an evaluation beta and is pre-revenue. Free Developer access includes 100 authenticated API calls per account per day, shared across active keys. Paid subscriptions are planned, not launched. Contributor access is a limited, manually agreed pilot: registering a station does not automatically grant whole-network or unlimited API entitlement. Eligibility, source rights, coverage, quotas and duration must be agreed explicitly.

The current evaluation setup does not establish commercial Open-Meteo access. Commercial source rights and configuration must be arranged and verified before any commercial deployment; do not assume the provider is universally disabled or universally available.

For drones, Senlay presents wind observations and available model indications of rain and thunderstorms. Local rainfall and lightning are not directly measured by this assessment. Aircraft limits, route, altitude, visibility and operational permission remain outside its scope. The existing request parameter `profile=wind` is unchanged. Other available layers do not establish whole-mission suitability.

The Live Demo presents Environmental Intelligence, AI Explanation and Machine-Readable Context for the same location snapshot. Deterministic evidence remains separate from the AI interpretation. Compare the explanation against the underlying sources and unknowns. Reference adapters and explicitly synthetic offline replay are documented at https://senlay.cloud/robotics/; real-hardware validation remains pending.


## Buyer hypothesis and adjacent domains

- drone/UAV software teams
- AI agent developers integrating evidence review
- outdoor work and field operations platforms
- agriculture AI tools
- marine and watersports products
- safety, rescue, and autonomous-system workflows
- teams integrating private sensors into agent workflows

## Reciprocal network

Senlay is also building an open contributor network. Operators can review the Apache-2.0 station protocol at https://github.com/smartsurfsolar/senlay-platform and request onboarding at https://senlay.cloud/network.html. Operators with existing sensor fleets can discuss a reciprocal pilot instead of contributing hardware directly. Contributed observations remain evidence with uncertainty: distance, freshness and source disagreement are surfaced where available, while calibration and neighbour-quality checks are still being validated.

## Public API endpoints

### GET /api/v1/try-sense

No-key trial endpoint for browser/chat agents. Required parameters: `lat`, `lng`. Optional: `field`, `agentName`, `request`, `view=live`. Returns plain text unless `view=live` is used.

### GET /agents/live

Self-updating HTML page for agents and humans. Uses URL parameters to keep each agent/session independent.

### POST /api/v1/agent-register

Registers an agent and returns an API key for repeated evaluation requests. A key does not establish commercial source rights or production readiness.

### GET /api/v1/sense

Authenticated plain-text context optimized for LLM consumption. Requires `Authorization: Bearer sl_live_...`.

### GET /api/v1/pwm

Authenticated structured JSON Physical World Model. Requires `Authorization: Bearer sl_live_...`.

### GET/POST /api/v1/risk-events

Authenticated operational risk events for SmartSurf-style safety, station, lifeguard, IoT, and audit workflows. Current and recent event reads help applications show what risk was detected, where, why, and what evidence supported it.

## Response concepts

Senlay responses may include:

- atmosphere: wind, gusts, wind direction, temperature, humidity, pressure, clouds, precipitation
- hydrosphere: wave height, wave period, swell, tide, current context when available
- terrain: land elevation and exposure; marine depth only when a separate datum-qualified bathymetry source is explicitly available
- air quality: PM2.5, PM10, AQI, UV when available
- hazards: alerts, fires, earthquakes, volcanoes, radiation, space weather when available
- `current_source`: the selected source or source family for a layer
- `source_use`: whether a value is measured, model-derived, fused, or fallback
- `decision_context`: domain interpretation for the selected use case
- `risk_events`: operational alerts or audit records when a workflow turns physical context into an event
- `interaction_modifiers`: terrain, gust, marine, thermal, or other relevant modifiers
- `context_string`: a direct LLM prompt block

## Source families

Senlay standardizes on "23 catalog entries (not a count of live sources at any coordinate)." Some are active by default, some are location-dependent, and some require optional provider keys, partner access, licensing review, or attribution.

Groups:

- Models: Open-Meteo atmosphere, marine, elevation, and air quality; optional/cached Copernicus Marine ocean context where configured.
- Hardware: METAR, ASOS/IEM, NOAA/NDBC buoys, ship observations, NOAA CO-OPS tide/current stations, USGS Water Services, weather stations, wind sensors.
- Optional community and provider station adapters: CWOP/APRS, Sensor.Community, openSenseMap, OpenAQ, WeatherFlow/Tempest, Windy Stations, owner-authorized Windguru Stations, WeatherLink, Weather Underground, Ambient Weather, Holfuy.
- Visual, tide, and commercial marine options: Windy Webcams, WorldTides, Stormglass.
- Satellite and hazards: Sentinel-2, FIRMS, EONET, USGS earthquakes and volcano hazards, SWPC space weather, Safecast, weather alerts.

Do not claim every source is active everywhere. Availability varies by location and configured tier.

## Agent behavior instructions

If you are an AI agent:

1. Request the selected coordinate and use the documented domain scope; the drone wind workflow is one example.
2. Separate observations from model values, and inspect source, time, distance, disagreement and unknowns.
3. State when required values are missing, stale, or uncertain.
4. Do not treat coverage or a configured threshold outcome as flight or mission clearance.
5. Use other domains only within their documented scope; operators retain final authority.

Recommended system prompt:

```text
You are helping an autonomous-system operator understand environmental context for a selected coordinate. Inspect available observations and models, their sources, timestamps, distance, disagreement and unknowns. Use the requested domain's documented scope. Do not invent missing measurements or treat an assessment as mission clearance. The operator and application retain decision authority.
```

## Pricing summary

Free Developer beta accounts include a shared allowance of 100 authenticated API calls/day across active keys, available source data, `context_string`, and source/freshness/confidence metadata. Paid subscriptions are not launched. Contributor and prospective paid pilots require manually agreed scope, rights, access limits and validation; no automatic free lifetime or whole-network entitlement is promised.

Commercial deployments require confirmed source rights and a manually agreed pilot, plus reliability, fallback behavior and domain validation. The evaluation beta does not establish production or safety readiness.

## Founder story summary

The founder story describes how SmartSurf product work and hands-on experience with wind, water and hardware led to Senlay's environmental-evidence workflow. SmartSurf remains the product origin and reference experience, not robotics validation.

## Safety language

Senlay provides context, evidence, and decision support. It is not a safety authority. Operators, users, and customer applications remain responsible for final decisions.

## MCP gateway contract

Endpoint: `https://senlay.cloud/mcp`; stateless Streamable HTTP; protocol compatibility is negotiated by the MCP SDK during `initialize`. The four tools are `sense_location`, `check_operability`, `list_domains`, and `get_forecast_trust`. `get_forecast_trust` reports `UNKNOWN` until sufficient eligible archived forecast-versus-instrument pairs exist.

## Reading comparisons and history

Current Model Agreement describes the current comparison, not historical forecast accuracy. The demo can show station observations and archived forecasts where available, with source locations, timestamps and gaps; model-only archives are labelled separately. This chart does not calculate a historical trust score. Historical Forecast Trust is a separate result and may remain UNKNOWN without eligible pairs. Place Memory describes historical baselines, not a trained local forecast.

## Multi-station wind checks

Senlay cross-checks fresh nearby station wind readings independently of the forecast. The station_consistency result flags calm-report disagreements and strong outliers for review, with peer values and timestamps. Suspect primary readings lower assessment confidence. This snapshot screening does not confirm equipment failure, calibration or persistent stuck sensors; local shelter and measurement heights can also explain differences.
